title: Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers: Telephone Fee on Call-Center Redemptions
content:
Reservations and Loyalty desk rule note on the telephone fee for Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers.

**1. When the fee arises.** A redemption through the reservations call center is charged a telephone fee, as a separate fee entry linked to that redemption. No fee is charged where the instrument cannot be redeemed online, or where the customer's Summit tier in the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program waives credit service fees. A waived fee is not recorded.

**2. Which redemption owes it.** A telephone fee is owed only for the latest call-center redemption on the credit, and only while no telephone fee entry is linked to it. An earlier call-center redemption that was left unbilled when a later call-center redemption was made is no longer owed a telephone fee.

**3. Amount.** The telephone fee is one amount in US dollars to the cent. It is the fee basis multiplied once by the combined rate, and only that product is rounded to the nearest cent.
- The **fee basis** is the instrument's telephone redemption fee per ticket, as a flat amount.
- The **combined rate** is one figure: the telephone-fee rates multiplied with one another. A combined rate of 1 leaves the fee equal to its basis.

## Which redemption owes a fee (hypothetical value histories)

| Call-center redemptions on the credit, oldest first | Telephone fee entries linked | Owed |
|---|---|---|
| one redemption on 3 March | none | the 3 March redemption |
| one redemption on 3 March | one, linked to 3 March | nothing |
| redemptions on 3 March and 9 May | none | the 9 May redemption only; 3 March is no longer owed |
| redemption on 3 March, then an online redemption on 9 May | none | the 3 March redemption, still the latest call-center one |
| any, on an instrument that cannot be redeemed online | none | nothing; no fee is charged |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

On an instrument whose telephone redemption fee is 25 US dollars, with a combined rate of 1, the fee is 25 multiplied by 1, which is 25.00. It is booked as one fee entry linked to the redemption that owes it.
